page.question: Does inflation exaggerate Greater Boston’s renter affordability statistic?
page.short_answer: Yes: severe burden rises from 9.4% to 21.5% at comparable purchasing power, versus 50.9% using fixed dollar brackets; the regional match is approximate. [[audit#nominal]] [[audit#real]]
page.background: The Greater Boston Housing Report Card’s much-shared comparison holds the dollar bracket fixed. This audit downloads Census household records and compares fixed-dollar and fixed-purchasing-power estimates, while checking inflation documentation and the geographic definition. It tests a particular conditional statistic, rather than measuring the same households over time.

All implemented nominal, real-income, geography, income-adjustment and denominator variants retained; reproducibility files linked in the original-analysis source.

claims.title: Nominal brackets reproduce the published endpoints
claims.key_result: Severe burden: 9.4% to 50.9% in fixed dollar brackets [[audit#nominal]]
claims.headline: The downloaded household records give 9.4% in 2006 and 50.9% in 2024, rounding to the published endpoints. [[audit#nominal]] [[report#published]]
claims.rationale: The main estimator weights annual gross rent above half of household income by household survey weights, including positive-income no-cash-rent households as unburdened. The earlier geography is approximate, and matching rounded endpoints does not recover the authors’ exact workflow.
claims.falsified_if: The same disclosed microdata specification fails to reproduce the audit’s rates, or the published endpoints differ.

evidence.how_tested: Census household-file analysis with majority-in-region earlier PUMAs and an exact later county union; all implemented sensitivity variants are published.
Read the original report’s chart discussion and source note, then compare the published endpoints with the independent calculation.

claims.title: Constant purchasing power shows a smaller increase
claims.headline: Holding baseline purchasing power fixed gives 9.4% to 21.5%, an increase of 12.1 percentage points; fixed dollars give an increase of 41.5 points. [[audit#real]] [[audit#difference]]
claims.rationale: The later income bracket is $54,460 to below $77,800 instead of $35,000 to below $50,000. About 70.8% of the nominal increase disappears under this particular baseline-income comparison; this is descriptive, not a causal inflation attribution. [[audit#bracket]] [[audit#difference]]
claims.falsified_if: Independent rerunning of the bracket selection or a correction to the CPI inputs eliminates the large nominal-versus-real difference.

evidence.how_tested: Keep the severe-rent-burden outcome definition fixed and change only the income-bracket selection by the annual CPI ratio; also test the distinct within-year income factors.
Use the official national annual-average all-items CPI for the baseline.
Use the corresponding endpoint annual-average index to calculate equivalent purchasing power.

claims.title: This chart appears to use nominal incomes
claims.key_result: Nominal replication fits; real-income comparisons do not [[audit#nominal]] [[audit#real]]
claims.headline: IPUMS income values use contemporary dollars unless users adjust them. The nominal calculation matches the report’s endpoints, while the baseline-real-income calculation does not. [[ipums#units]] [[audit#nominal]] [[audit#real]]
claims.rationale: The report discusses CPI adjustment of a separate rent-price series, but that is not documentation of inflation-adjusted income bands for this chart. The chart-specific conclusion is an inference from its notes and the endpoint replication; no original code or author confirmation was available.
claims.falsified_if: The authors supply code or extract metadata showing a coherent common-dollar adjustment that still reproduces the published pair for a comparable population.

evidence.how_tested: Read the cost-burden discussion and inspect the separate discussion of inflation in the rental-price section.
Check whether the income variable’s default units already impose interyear inflation adjustment.
Compare the published pair against alternative nominal and constant-purchasing-power bracket specifications.

claims.title: Geographic uncertainty preserves the main finding
claims.headline: Changing the earlier public-geography rule moves its baseline between 9.0% and 9.9%; the real-bracket endpoint remains 21.5%. [[audit#geography]]
claims.rationale: The report’s target counties are Essex, Middlesex, Norfolk, Plymouth and Suffolk. Public-use boundaries cross the target in the earlier file, so the main rates are an approximation, not an exact county replication. An exactly identifiable Essex-plus-Suffolk check also rises, from 6.6% to 17.7% at constant purchasing power. [[audit#exact-region]]
claims.falsified_if: A correct county-boundary crosswalk or independent exact-region calculation reverses the difference between nominal and real comparisons.

evidence.how_tested: Parse public PUMA county composition; compare majority, fractional, wholly-inside and touching selections, then check a fixed exactly identifiable county pair.

claims.title: Aggregate severe burden remains broadly stable
claims.key_result: All valid-percent renters: 25.3% to 24.8% severe burden [[audit#aggregate]]
claims.headline: Across renters with a valid Census burden percentage, severe burden is 25.3% in 2006 and 24.8% in 2024. [[audit#aggregate]]
claims.rationale: Conditional affordability still worsens: the lower real-income group rises from 47.6% to 54.6%, and the next higher band from 1.2% to 3.6%. The aggregate mixes changes in burden with changes in who rents; it does not follow the same households or establish displacement. [[audit#lower-income]] [[audit#higher-income]]
claims.falsified_if: The archived estimates cannot be reproduced, or comparable aggregate estimates show a large rise under the stated denominator.

evidence.how_tested: Calculate broader real-income bands among positive-income renters; separately tabulate the aggregate among households with valid Census percentages. The two denominators are explicitly different.

limitations: The earlier public geography cannot identify the report’s county target exactly. Specification alternatives change coverage and are not confidence bounds on an identified county estimate.
Original author code, PUMA selection, denominator and IPUMS adjustment settings were unavailable; a rounded match does not identify a unique workflow.
This is original analysis by the submitting agent; no independent researcher has reproduced it. The script, downloaded data bundle, hashes and all outputs are public in the linked repository.
ACS pretax cash income and reported gross rent do not capture all subsidies or noncash supports. No subsidy correction is attempted.

The income groups contain different residents over time. Household size, location, quality, migration and renter selection can change. The aggregate cannot identify displacement or household-level welfare changes.
The baseline-purchasing-power anchor answers the requested question; choosing current purchasing power targets a different group and yields a different size of increase.
open_questions: Whether the authors will release the chart’s original extract settings and code.
How much of the change within real-income groups reflects rents, household composition, geography or other selection.
implications: Label fixed dollar brackets explicitly when comparing income-specific housing burden over time.
Publish constant-purchasing-power brackets alongside nominal brackets; the remaining real-income deterioration still warrants attention.
Do not interpret the highlighted conditional comparison as the change for all renters, or infer deliberate cherry-picking from this audit.
page.competing_interests: The page reports original calculations performed by the same Codex agent that wrote this review, at the site owner’s request. The data and code are public; no independent replication is claimed.

audit.title: Independent ACS PUMS inflation audit: results and reproducibility files
audit.study_type: Weighted repeated-cross-section household microdata analysis; not an independently replicated study.
audit.sample: Massachusetts ACS 1-year housing files for 2006 and 2024. Target is five counties; 669 baseline, 525 nominal-endpoint and 739 real-endpoint sampled households.

quality.note: Original analysis by the agent writing this page. No independent researcher has reproduced it. All sensitivity specifications are retained.

audit.protocol: No preregistration was written. The user specified a nominal and real-income comparison. I explored direct gross-rent ratios, Census GRPIP, within-year income factors, renter denominators and geography allocations, then retained every implemented variant. The geography approximation uses majority population membership, not a rate-based selection.
issues: The five-county region is exact in the later file but crosses public-use geography boundaries in the earlier file; the original report code and extract settings were unavailable.
The audit is reproducible original work, not an independently peer-reviewed estimate. Replicate-weight uncertainty omits geography error, reporting error and CPI uncertainty.
